exposure: Amniotic fluid discordance (AFD) (intertwin difference of >=3 cm in maximal vertical pocket measurement)
outcome: Composite neonatal morbidity (respiratory distress syndrome, intraventricular hemorrhage grades 3 and 4, necrotizing enterocolitis or sepsis)
cohort: The study cohort consisted of 34 monochorionic diamniotic (MCDA) twin pregnancies with amniotic fluid discordance, compared to a control group of 101 MCDA twin pregnancies without amniotic fluid discordance, twin to twin transfusion syndrome, or selective intrauterine growth restriction.
finding: Monochorionic diamniotic twins with amniotic fluid discordance are at increased risk for developing twin anemia-polycythemia sequence (20.6% vs 0%), earlier delivery (34.6 weeks vs 35.8 weeks), and significantly higher rates of composite neonatal morbidity (13.2% vs 2.5%).
gest_age: AFD group delivered at 34.6 weeks, control group delivered at 35.8 weeks.
